documented.v 55 lines

  1. // A small register file wrapper, written to exercise the documentation
  2. // view: every kind of comment the frontends record ends up somewhere on
  3. // the generated page.
  4. //
  5. // The leading block above a module becomes its description; the comment
  6. // after a port becomes that port's note.
  7. module documented #(
  8. parameter WIDTH = 8, // width of the stored word
  9. parameter DEPTH = 4 // number of words
  10. ) (
  11. input wire clk, // rising-edge clock for every port
  12. input wire rst_n, // active-low asynchronous reset
  13. input wire we, // write enable, one word per cycle
  14. input wire [1:0] addr, // word selected for read and write
  15. input wire [WIDTH-1:0] din, // word written while `we` is high
  16. output reg [WIDTH-1:0] dout, // registered read port
  17. output wire busy // high on the cycle after a write
  18. );
  20. // The storage itself; inference turns this into a memory with one
  21. // read port and one write port.
  22. reg [WIDTH-1:0] words [0:DEPTH-1];
  24. // One flag, set by a write and cleared the cycle after.
  25. reg written;
  27. always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
  28. if (!rst_n) begin
  29. dout <= {WIDTH{1'b0}};
  30. written <= 1'b0;
  31. end else begin
  32. if (we) begin
  33. words[addr] <= din;
  34. end
  35. dout <= words[addr];
  36. written <= we;
  37. end
  38. end
  40. assign busy = written;
  42. endmodule
  44. // A plain adder, instantiated by nothing here, so the index shows more
  45. // than one module and the schematic of a leaf.
  46. module documented_adder #(
  47. parameter W = 4 // operand width
  48. ) (
  49. input wire [W-1:0] a, // first operand
  50. input wire [W-1:0] b, // second operand
  51. output wire [W-1:0] y // sum, truncated to W bits
  52. );
  53. assign y = a + b;
  54. endmodule
